storage: local Docker named volume; loopback HTTP; no TLS or artificial network delay
limitations: Short probes identify candidate rates, not sustained or 30-day capacity.
SDK events and adapter wire output are recorded once, then replayed with new identities.
Verification retains compact replay descriptions; complete expected payloads are reconstructed and compared after restart.
OTLP batching and gzip model a gateway; SDK adapters still send one event per request.
Request latency starts after serialization/compression; preparation and schedule lag are reported separately.
Resource sampling includes Docker exec overhead and may miss peaks. Container memory includes filesystem cache.
Scheduled retention scans run every five seconds with a 30-day TTL; these runs do not measure deletion of expired data.
Image ID identifies the executable. Git source provenance is the local checkout and cannot attest to a separately supplied image.
The 13 development containers were stopped for both measured conditions and restored afterward. Other host applications remained running.
Both conditions start from the same checkpointed preload. Profiles exclude preload and final checkpoint. Read-worker profiles are reported separately.
Dashboard reads use a loop that waits one second after completion and resource sampling. Faster completion can produce more read requests in the same traffic window.
Queue backlog is sampled; peaks between samples can be missed. An already empty queue makes drain_ms primarily status-request overhead.
This is one shared-worker/separate-reader pair in that order on a shared Mac, with only 25 or 26 samples per dashboard endpoint. No sustained capacity or statistical significance is established.
